say: Do not guess shrinkage. Wash and dry a 20 cm square as the client will, then measure. If it is now 19 cm, it shrank 5 percent. Pre-wash, or add that to your lengths.

say: Always test the iron on a scrap first. Cotton takes a hot iron, but many laces, sequinned fabrics and synthetic linings melt or pucker at high heat.

cards.d: Cotton takes a hot iron. Many laces, sequins and synthetic linings melt at high heat.
Put plain cotton between the iron and delicate or shiny fabrics. Never press sequins.
Lift and lower the iron. Sliding it stretches fitted garments out of shape.

say: Use a press cloth, a piece of plain cotton, between the iron and delicate or shiny fabric. Never press directly on sequins or metallic threads.

cards.d: Cotton takes a hot iron. Many laces, sequins and synthetic linings melt at high heat.
Put plain cotton between the iron and delicate or shiny fabrics. Never press sequins.
Lift and lower the iron. Sliding it stretches fitted garments out of shape.

say: Press by lifting and lowering the iron, not sliding it, so fitted garments do not stretch. Press every seam as you sew.

say: Grading makes a pattern larger or smaller in a planned way. It is not photocopying it bigger. In real bodies, the bust, waist and hip change a lot between sizes. In this example chart, 4 cm each.
But the neck, shoulder and length change only a little. Enlarge everything by 10 percent and the dress gapes at the neckline. Build your own size chart from your real clients.
For example, Kemi's tested size L block is the base for 25 aso-ebi gowns. Six women measure close to XL.

say: A specification lists what the finished garment should measure. A tolerance is how far it may vary and still pass. For example, Grace in Port Harcourt allows 0.5 cm on girths and 1 cm on lengths.

2 cm seam allowance left: re-sew 0.4 cm out

say: Gown 14 should measure 104 cm at the bust, 86 at the waist and 110 at the hip.

say: She measures it flat. Bust and waist pass, but the hip is 108.5 cm. That is 1.5 cm small, so it fails.

say: There is 2 cm of seam allowance left, so she re-sews each side seam 0.4 cm closer to the edge at the hip.

say: The hip is now 110.1 cm. It passes, and the problem was found in her shop, not on the wedding morning.

say: Check every garment against these five points before it leaves your shop.
Write the result in a quality log, so you can see which faults keep coming back.
